shorts.title: Why Is the Pronghorn So Fast When Nothing Can Catch It? 🦌
shorts.description:
This animal runs fifty-five miles an hour. Pronghorns aren't antelopes, and they shed their horn sheaths every year.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: Pronghorn: Jan Ebr & Ivana Ebrová (CC BY), Daniel S. Katz (CC BY), CC0. creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
shorts.comment: What did you guess it was running from?

shorts.title: A Giraffe's Tongue Is Black and 45 cm Long 🦒
shorts.description:
A giraffe's tongue is black. Fully grown giraffes stand 4.3-5.7 m (14-19 ft) tall.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: Giraffe: Tia Offner (CC BY), Darren Obbard (CC BY), Tom Heijnen (CC BY). creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
shorts.comment: Could you sleep only 4 and a half hours?

shorts.title: The Shoebill Stands Still Until You Forget It's There 🐦
shorts.description:
This bird hunts by not moving. Only about 5,000-8,000 shoebills are thought to be left in the wild.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: Shoebill: William Stephens (CC BY), Michael Bakker Paiva (CC BY). creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
shorts.comment: Who would win a staring contest?

shorts.title: Each Tarsier Eye Is as Big as Its Brain 👀
shorts.description:
Each eye is as big as its brain. Philippine tarsiers can call at a dominant frequency of 70 kHz, ultrasound to us.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: Tarsier: CC0, desertnaturalist (CC BY). creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0

shorts.title: This Squirrel's Body Drops Below Freezing ❄️
shorts.description:
This squirrel's body drops below freezing. Hibernation lasts seven to eight months, from late summer to April.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: Arctic ground squirrel: Julien Renoult (CC BY), Валерия Ковалева (CC BY), CC0, Matt Muir (CC BY). creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0

shorts.title: Wild Turkeys Sleep in Trees 🦃
shorts.description:
Wild turkeys sleep in trees. A tom's head can turn red, blue or white with his mood; white means most excited.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: Wild turkey: Brooke J. (CC BY), CC0, Kristin M. Tolle (CC BY). creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
shorts.comment: Did you know turkeys could fly?

shorts.title: A 2,000-Pound Bison Can Run 40 MPH 🦬
shorts.description:
This animal weighs a ton. Runs forty mph. There were roughly 31,000 wild bison as of March 2019.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: American bison: CC0, Syd Cannings (CC BY). creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
shorts.comment: Would you get out of the car?

shorts.title: Roadrunners Eat Rattlesnakes 🐍
shorts.description:
Roadrunners eat rattlesnakes. Roadrunners get rid of extra salt through glands in their nose.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: Greater roadrunner: Jody Shugart (CC BY), Norman Kuring (CC BY), MarvalPhotography19 (CC BY), Matt Felperin (CC BY). creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0

shorts.title: Brown Pelicans Dive Headfirst From 60 Feet 🐦
shorts.description:
This bird dives headfirst from sixty feet. Gulls sometimes try to steal the pelican's catch.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: Brown pelican: Jay Pruett (CC BY), CC0, ajott (CC BY), Don Loarie (CC BY). creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
shorts.comment: Would you try a sixty-foot dive?

shorts.title: The Snake Bird Swims With Only Its Neck Out 🐍
shorts.description:
This bird swims like a snake. Anhingas toss speared fish into the air and swallow them headfirst.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: Anhinga: Shiva Shenoy (CC BY), Jonathan Layman (CC BY). creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0

shorts.title: Red-Eyed Tree Frog Eggs Hatch Early to Escape Snakes 🐸
shorts.description:
These frog eggs can hatch early on purpose. Undisturbed, the eggs usually hatch in 6-8 days.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: Red-eyed tree frog: Brian Gratwicke (CC BY), Luke Padon (CC BY), John G. Phillips (CC BY). creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
